force, velocity, distance, mass
mass, energy, temperature, momentum
weight, acceleration, momentum, speed

questions.questionText:

The table shows the distances moved by each object in each second of its motion.
Which object is moving with constant non-zero acceleration?
distance moved distance moved distance moved distance moved
in 1st second/m in 2nd second/m in 3rd second/m in 4th second/m

The drag force on a car increases with speed. At 20m/s, the total drag force is 400N. The mass
of the car is 1200kg and the driving force is constant at 700N.
Which statement about the acceleration of the car at 20m/s is correct?

options.text: The acceleration is 0.25m/s2 but will decrease as time passes.
The acceleration is 0.25m/s2 but will increase as time passes.
The acceleration is 0.58m/s2 but will decrease as time passes.
The acceleration is 0.58m/s2 but will increase as time passes.

questions.questionText:
The momentum of a body is changed by a force acting on it for a period of time.
Which action increases the change in momentum?

options.text: doubling the force and halving the time
doubling the force for the same time
halving both the force and the time
halving the force and doubling the time

∆E = Y × Z × ∆h
where ∆E is the change in gravitational energy and ∆h is the change in height.
Which row gives the quantities Y and Z?
Y Z

gravitational field strength density

speed mass

newton
volt
watt

A sample of gas is trapped in a rigid container. As the temperature of the gas is increased, the
pressure increases.
Which statement is not correct?

options.text: The gas molecules have greater kinetic energy.
The gas molecules hit the walls of the container harder.
The gas molecules hit the walls of the container more frequently.
The gas molecules move further apart.

questions.questionText: What happens when the temperature of a liquid increases?

options.text: The mass of the liquid increases, making the liquid less dense.
The mass of the liquid increases, making the liquid more dense.
The volume of the liquid increases, making the liquid less dense.
The volume of the liquid increases, making the liquid more dense.

questions.questionText:
A bar of metal, which is a good thermal conductor, is heated at one end.
What is the main method of transfer of thermal energy along the bar?

options.text: lattice vibration
movement of atoms of the metal along the bar
transfer by electrons
vibration of atoms of the metal bar

f f

questions.questionText:
The diagram shows a bar magnet at rest on a smooth horizontal surface. A length of soft-iron
wire is held parallel to the magnet.
soft-iron wire
magnet
The wire is released.
What happens?

options.text: The wire moves away from the magnet.
The wire moves towards the magnet.
The wire’s centre stays in its present position and the wire rotates through 90° in a clockwise direction.
The wire’s centre stays in its present position and the wire rotates through 90° in an anticlockwise direction.

questions.questionText:

same material as the standard wire, but of different lengths and diameters.
Which wire would definitely have a resistance of less than the standard wire?
wire length wire diameter

options.text: longer larger
longer smaller
shorter larger
shorter smaller

questions.questionText:
A wire is moved across a magnetic field. This causes an induced current in the wire.
The induced current interacts with the magnetic field to produce a force on the wire.
In which direction is this force?

options.text: in the direction of the current
in the direction of movement of the wire
in the opposite direction to the current
in the opposite direction to the movement of the wire

questions.questionText:
The energy generated in stable stars comes from nuclear reactions.
Which type of reaction occurs in the Sun?

options.text: Helium nuclei break up to give hydrogen nuclei.
Helium nuclei join together to form hydrogen nuclei.
Hydrogen nuclei break up to give helium nuclei.
Hydrogen nuclei join together to form helium nuclei.
